summary: This is a first-pass evidence summary on tonsillitis and acute pharyngitis, covering etiology, diagnosis (Centor/McIsaac criteria), antibiotic and steroid treatment, tonsillectomy indications, and complications (peritonsillar abscess, rheumatic fever, PANDAS). It synthesizes 15 published sources retrieved via PubMed and is not a systematic review. The document is a clinical literature scan with no direct relevance to a biotech/drug development TRL assessment, as it does not describe a novel therapeutic, device, or technology under development.

content_blocks.title: Document Metadata and Scope
content_blocks.content: Status: first-pass literature scan, not a systematic review. Scope: etiology (viral vs. bacterial/GAS), diagnosis (Centor/McIsaac), treatment (antibiotics, rapid testing, steroids), tonsillectomy indications, and complications (peritonsillar abscess, rheumatic fever, PANDAS). Access date: 2026-09-04. Method: paper-lookup skill ('K-Dense' literature-search tool), PubMed E-utilities (esearch/esummary/efetch), cross-checked against Unpaywall for open-access status.

content_blocks.title: Etiology Summary
content_blocks.content: Most acute pharyngitis/tonsillitis is viral. Group A β-hemolytic streptococcus (GAS/GABHS) is the dominant bacterial cause, accounting for roughly 25% of pharyngitis episodes in children (lower in adults), per Pellegrino et al. (2023) multi-guideline comparison. This figure is a single-source approximation from a guideline-comparison paper, not a directly verified primary epidemiological measurement.

content_blocks.title: Diagnosis — Centor and McIsaac Criteria
content_blocks.content: Centor criteria (1981): tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical adenopathy, absence of cough, history of fever — derived from logistic regression in adult ER patients. Probability of positive GAS culture: 2.5% with 0 criteria, 56% with all 4. McIsaac et al. (1998) added age adjustment (+1 for ages 3–14, −1 for ≥45), validated against throat culture in 521 patients; score-based management reduced antibiotic prescribing by 48% vs. usual care without increasing culture use. Rapid antigen detection tests (alone or combined with clinical score) cut antibiotic prescription rates by an absolute 25 percentage points (95% CI 18–31) vs. clinical judgment alone across 5 RCTs (Cohen et al., Cochrane 2020); evidence that this changes dispensed antibiotics or complication rates is low- to very-low-certainty.

content_blocks.title: Treatment — Antibiotics (Cochrane Review)
content_blocks.content: Cochrane review (Spinks, Glasziou & Del Mar, 2021): 29 placebo-controlled trials, 15,337 cases. Antibiotics reduce sore throat at day 3 (RR 0.70) and day 7 (RR 0.50), reduce suppurative complications (otitis media, quinsy/peritonsillar abscess), and reduce acute rheumatic fever risk (Peto OR 0.36). Caveat: most trials predate modern rheumatic-fever epidemiology; 82% of untreated patients were symptom-free within a week. Penicillin/amoxicillin remain first-line; clindamycin preferred for penicillin-allergic patients (IDSA 2012 guideline, Shulman et al.).

content_blocks.title: Treatment — Corticosteroids for Symptom Relief
content_blocks.content: de Cassan et al. (Cochrane 2020): 9 small trials, 1,319 participants (mostly adults). Corticosteroids added to usual care roughly doubled the chance of complete pain resolution at 24 hours (RR 2.4) and 1.5x at 48 hours; NNT ≈5 to prevent one person still in pain at 24h. Limited safety reporting; evidence base is small.

content_blocks.title: Tonsillectomy Indications — Paradise Criteria and AAO-HNS Guideline
content_blocks.content: AAO-HNS pediatric guideline (Mitchell et al., 2019, update of 2011): surgical referral threshold ('Paradise criteria'): ≥7 episodes in past year, ≥5/year for 2 years, or ≥3/year for 3 years, each documented with fever >38.3°C, cervical adenopathy, tonsillar exudate, or positive GAS test. Below threshold, watchful waiting is a strong recommendation. Paradise et al. RCTs (1984, severely affected children; 2002, moderately affected children): tonsillectomy significantly reduced throat-infection incidence in first 1–2 postoperative years; 14% of surgical patients had self-limited surgical complications. Cochrane review (Burton et al., 2014): benefit is modest — children average 3.0 vs. 3.6 sore-throat episodes in first postoperative year (one of the surgical group's three being the predictable postop episode). Evidence in adults is low-quality and insufficient for firm conclusions.

content_blocks.title: Complications — Peritonsillar Abscess (PTA)
content_blocks.content: Galluzzi & Garavello (2024) systematic review: 12 studies, 2,211 pediatric cases, all retrospective. Incision-and-drainage plus antibiotics is dominant treatment (69% of cases); antibiotics alone in 16.4%; recurrence rate 2–15.8%, generally within 1–2 months.

content_blocks.title: Complications — Rheumatic Fever
content_blocks.content: AHA revised Jones criteria (Gewitz et al., 2015): current diagnostic reference for acute rheumatic fever. First major revision since 1992. Added Doppler echocardiography as a tool for diagnosing (including subclinical) carditis and stratifying criteria by population risk.

content_blocks.title: Complications — PANDAS
content_blocks.content: Nielsen et al. (2019) systematic review/meta-analysis: 3 studies, 82 PANDAS cases vs. 127 controls. No significantly increased rate of GAS infection in PANDAS cases (RR 0.99). No significant temporal association between GAS infection and symptom exacerbation (RR 2.33, 95% CI 0.63–8.70, not significant). PANDAS cases did have more neuropsychiatric exacerbations in general (RR 1.54). Conclusion: PANDAS is a contested, evolving hypothesis; the core mechanistic claim lacks strong supporting evidence as of 2017 (search cutoff). Evidence base is small and methodologically heterogeneous.

content_blocks.title: Sources Table — Citations and Relevance
content_blocks.content:
15 sources cited:
1. Centor et al. (1981) — original Centor criteria derivation study. PMID 6763125.
2. McIsaac et al. (1998) — McIsaac (age-adjusted Centor) score validation. PMID 9475915. Open access (PMC).
3. McIsaac et al. (2004) — score-guided management outcomes. PMID 15069046.
4. Cohen et al. (Cochrane 2020) — rapid antigen/PCR test-guided prescribing. PMID 32497279. Open access.
5. Spinks, Glasziou & Del Mar (Cochrane 2021) — antibiotics vs. placebo. PMID 34881426. Open access.
6. de Cassan et al. (Cochrane 2020) — corticosteroids for sore throat. PMID 32356360. Open access.
7. Shulman et al. (IDSA 2012) — antibiotic choice/dosing. PMID 23091044. Not open access.
8. Pellegrino et al. (2023) — guideline comparison, etiology prevalence. PMID 37819417. Open access.
9. Paradise et al. (1984) — original Paradise criteria RCT, severely affected children. PMID 6700642. Not open access.
10. Paradise et al. (2002) — RCT, moderately affected children. PMID 12093941. Not open access.
11. Burton et al. (Cochrane 2014) — tonsillectomy vs. non-surgical treatment. PMID 25407135. Open access.
12. Mitchell et al. (AAO-HNS 2019) — current surgical-referral threshold guideline. PMID 30798778. Not open access.
13. Galluzzi & Garavello (2024) — PTA management and recurrence. PMID 39685823. Open access.
14. Gewitz et al. (AHA 2015) — Jones criteria revision. PMID 25908771. Open access.
15. Nielsen et al. (2019) — PANDAS strep-exacerbation meta-analysis. PMID 30325890. Not open access.

content_blocks.title: Flags / Caveats
content_blocks.content:
Key limitations flagged by the authors:
- Search is targeted, not exhaustive (PubMed only; Cochrane Library interface, Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex not separately queried; NICE guidance not retrieved directly).
- 'Paradise criteria' is a community label; numeric thresholds sourced from AAO-HNS guideline (source #12), not verified against original 1984/2002 trial full text (abstracts only retrieved).
- PANDAS evidence is thin (3 studies, 82 cases); finding is mixed, not a clean negative.
- Rheumatic fever prevention evidence (Cochrane source #5) dominated by 1950s trials; Peto OR 0.36 should not be extrapolated to contemporary low-incidence populations.
- Rapid-test evidence on complications is very low/low certainty (complications OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.03–26.65); only 'rapid tests reduce prescribing' is reasonably well supported.
- '~25% GAS in children' is a single-source figure from a guideline-comparison paper, not a primary epidemiological study.
- Full text not retrieved for any non-open-access source; all claims from those sources are from abstracts only.

content_blocks.title: Provenance / Methodology
content_blocks.content: Retrieval type: targeted topic scan across 5 subtopics (etiology, diagnosis, treatment, tonsillectomy, complications), not exhaustive/systematic. Databases: PubMed (esearch + esummary + efetch/abstract) for all 15 sources; Unpaywall (DOI lookup) for OA status of 8 sources lacking PMC IDs. No NCBI API key used (rate-limited to 3 req/s). No pagination needed. Cochrane Library's own interface not queried directly. NICE and other national guidelines not retrieved as primary documents. All synthesis is from structured abstracts via PubMed efetch.

key_findings: Document is a clinical evidence summary on tonsillitis/acute pharyngitis — not a biotech/drug development document; TRL relevance is low.
GAS accounts for ~25% of pharyngitis episodes in children; most acute pharyngitis is viral.
Centor criteria: GAS culture probability ranges from 2.5% (0 criteria) to 56% (all 4 criteria); McIsaac age-adjusted score reduced antibiotic prescribing by 48% in 521-patient validation.
Rapid antigen tests reduce antibiotic prescription rates by 25 percentage points (95% CI 18–31) vs. clinical judgment alone (5 RCTs, Cochrane 2020); evidence on complications is very low certainty.

Antibiotics reduce sore throat at day 3 (RR 0.70) and day 7 (RR 0.50), and reduce rheumatic fever risk (Peto OR 0.36) — but 82% of untreated patients recover within a week (Cochrane 2021, 29 trials, 15,337 cases).
Corticosteroids double complete pain resolution at 24h (RR 2.4), NNT ≈5; evidence from 9 small trials (1,319 participants) with limited safety data.
Tonsillectomy threshold (Paradise criteria): ≥7 episodes/year, ≥5/year×2, or ≥3/year×3; benefit is modest (3.0 vs. 3.6 sore-throat episodes in first postoperative year per Cochrane 2014).
Peritonsillar abscess: incision-and-drainage + antibiotics in 69% of cases; recurrence 2–15.8% (systematic review, 12 studies, 2,211 pediatric cases, 2024).
PANDAS: no significant GAS-exacerbation temporal link (RR 2.33, 95% CI 0.63–8.70, NS) in meta-analysis of 3 studies (82 cases); hypothesis remains contested.
All synthesis is from PubMed abstracts only; full text not retrieved for non-open-access sources; search is not exhaustive.
